articleTitle: Lesion Segmentation in Dermoscopic Images using Superpixel based Fast Fuzzy C-means Clustering
abstract: Dermoscopy is the widely used non-invasive diagnostic imaging modality for differentiation of various types of skin cancer. In this work, an attempt is made to segment the lesions in dermoscopic images using two different superpixel based segmentation approaches. The images are obtained from a publicly available database. Two different segmentation approaches namely Superpixel based Segmentation (SPS) and Superpixel based Fast Fuzzy C-Means Clustering (SPFFCM) segmentation are utilized for lesion segmentation in the dermoscopic images. The segmented regions are validated with the ground truth images provided in the database. Preliminary results of this pilot study are validated with six segmentation evaluation metrics namely Accuracy, Precision, F-Measure, Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC), Sensitivity, Specificity, Dice index and Jaccard index. Results show that SPFFCM has better segmentation results when compared to SPS method. Hence, it appears that SPFFCM could be used as an inbuilt segmentation tool for lesion segmentation in dermoscopic image processing.

articleTitle: Modulated Predictive Voltage Control of a Direct Matrix Converter
abstract: This paper proposes a modulated voltage control strategy based on the predictive control approach. To accomplish this, a direct matrix converter topology is used in combination with a three-phase generation system. Results based on a MATLAB/Simulink simulation environment are discussed and the most relevant characteristics of the proposed modulated predictive control approach are highlighted considering the total harmonic distortion as a performance parameter and complying with the specifications of the standards for uninterruptible power supplies. The root-mean-square error is also displayed to show the quality of the system signal.

articleTitle: Towards an Attention Mechanism LSTM Framework for Human Action Recognition in Videos
abstract: Action recognition in videos is currently a topic of interest in the area of computer vision, due to potential applications such as: multimedia indexing, surveillance in public spaces, among others. Attention mechanisms have become a very important concept within deep learning approach, their operation tries to imitate the visual capacity of people that allows them to focus their attention on relevant parts of a scene to extract important information. In this paper we propose a soft attention mechanism adapted to a base CNN–LSTM architecture. First, a VGG16 convolutional neural network extracts the features from the input video. Then an LSTM classifies the video into a particular class. To carry out the training and testing phases, we used the HMDB-51 and UCF-101 datasets. We evaluate the performance of our system using accuracy as an evaluation metric, obtaining 40.7% (base approach), 51.2% (with attention) for HMDB-51 and 75.8% (base approach), 87.2% (with attention) for UCF-101.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Voltage Stability of a Galapagos Microgrid using a DSTATCOM
abstract: A demographic growth of the Galapagos archipelago and the increase in the tourist sector have caused the massive use of air conditioning systems (A/C). The A/C is considered as dynamic loads of induction motor type. When these loads are massively connected to the electrical microgrid system (MG) of the Galapagos Islands: Baltra-Santa Cruz, they cause operational problems related to dynamic voltage stability and reactive power control. This situation gets worse when disturbances occur in the MG system. It becomes difficult to maintain voltage stability, the continuity and quality of the electric power supply. The aim of this paper is to demonstrate that with the incorporation of a Synchronous Static Compensating device for Distribution (DSTATCOM) in the MG Baltra-Santa Cruz system, the dynamic performance of the voltage and the supply of reactive power are improved when disturbances occur in a massive A/C connection scenario. This is done through dynamic simulations in PowerFactory DIgSilent. The results show that a coordinated operation of the generation system and the DSTATCOM device allows solving problems related to the instability of voltage and reactive power due to massive connection of inductive loads in the MG Baltra - Santa Cruz of Galapagos Islands.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis in PMSM with Partitioned Stator Windings−Part II: Interturn Short-Circuit and Static Eccentricity
abstract: A strategy for interturn short-circuits and static eccentricity diagnosis in permanent magnet synchronous ma-chines (PMSM) is proposed in this paper. In several practical implementations, the PMSM faults produce similar behavior patterns on electrical signals. In these cases, robust diagnostic strategies are required in order to identify the fault, without being influenced by external disturbances. To achieve this goal, a 2D model of PMSM was designed and evaluated by using of a finite element method (FEM). The fault diagnosis is realized by analyzing the behavior pattern of a residual voltages (RV) in the αβ plane. A PMSM prototype with modified stator windings and bearings with eccentric bushings was used to evaluate the proposed diagnosis strategy. Experimental results obtained with this PMSM demonstrate the correct fault diagnosis of both, interturn short-circuits and static eccentricity.

articleTitle: Application of quantum optimization techniques (QUBO method) to cargo logistics on ships and airplanes
abstract: The video (https://youtu.be/qB07ueMVw0w) presents our ongoing work on the optimization of cargo logistics processes with containers using quantum computing, mainly in airplanes and barges, of great international relevance. Combinatorial optimization problems are computationally complex in conventional computing. The origins of Quantum Computing date back to the early 90's. This discipline allows solving problems that in conventional computing are complex [1]. We present a Quantum Computing tool, the QUBO method (Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization) [2], which is suitable for formulating combinatorial optimization problems. QUBO is a recently developed tool, based on Quantum Annealing and is implemented in some current quantum computers. It consists of minimizing outputs of the type x<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</sup>Qx with x being a binary decision vector and Q a square or triangular matrix with constant parameters provided by the model. Restrictions can be added to the treated system. These problems have to do with making good decisions in environments where a large number of binary decisions (Yes/No) must be made and each set of decisions produces a corresponding objective function value, such as a cost or benefit value. In the video we also present the example of the Number Partitioning Problem.

articleTitle: ARAnimals: Mobile Application with Augmented Reality for the Learning of Vertebrate Animals
abstract: This work shows the results of an application of augmented reality for learning about vertebrate animals in preschool children. A mobile application with augmented reality, called ARAnimals, was implemented following the agile Scrum methodology. The research design was quasi-experimental, where the sample consisted of two classrooms of 5-year-old students from a private school in the city of Lima. The experimental group improved by 33.04% compared to the control group, which only improved by 14.56%. Furthermore, the difference in the average time it took to evaluate the subject in the experimental group and in the control group was significant. The time for the experimental group was 13.3 min., and the time for the control group was 16.7 min. It is concluded that the use of a mobile application with augmented reality satisfactorily influences the learning of vertebrate animals, specifically in four aspects that are included in the dimensions to which they correspond.

articleTitle: Antenna for Telemetry Data Relay Communications in LEO Satellites and Inmarsat-F4 Constellation
abstract: This research analyzes an approach to increase the radio link contact time of telemetry and telecommand data of low orbit satellites based on the data relay systems through Inmarsat-F4 GEO satellites constellation. For practical purposes, the orbital dynamics between a LEO and GEO satellites using TLE orbital parameters of the SAOCOM 1A satellite and Inmarsat-F4 constellation has been used. The results obtained allow us to determinate the radiation pattern characteristics that must be fulfilled by the proposed antenna. On the other hand, the link budget calculations shows that we could use an low gain antenna. In this way, an Conical Quadrifilar Helix Antenna with hemispherical radiation pattern in elevation angle, and omnidirectional in azimuth angle with Right Hand Circular Polarization (RHCP) has been designed. The main electrical parameters obtained are: HPBW: 198°, Axial Ratio (AR) lower 3dB with theta: −90° to 90°. |S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>|: -40dB@1.61Ghz. Bandwidth: 239 MHz.

articleTitle: Adaptive Backstepping Controller with Output Feedback for Dielectric Elastomer Actuator
abstract: This paper presents an output feedback backstepping controller for Dielectric Elastomer Actuator. The main challenges in the considered problem are the actuator nonlinearities and the output feedback. The control problem is solved by designing an observer with linear matrix inequalities technique and a controller with backstepping methodology. The stability analysis is performed for closed loop system by Lyapunov function. Furthermore, the adaptation is applied to obtain robustness for unknown load force. The presented approach is illustrated on simulations.

articleTitle: Toward Applying Fuzz Testing Techniques on the SUCHAI Nanosatellites Flight Software
abstract: The success of the CubeSat nanosatellites space missions depends on all systems ability to perform properly in a harsh environment. A key component in every space mission is the flight software, which manages all the processes that must be performed by the satellite on its onboard computer. Literature shows that CubeSat missions suffer high infant mortality and many spacecraft failures are related to flight software errors, some of them resulting in a complete mission loss. Extensive software testing is the primary tool used by flight software developers, to ensure code quality and avoid such failures. Nevertheless, CubeSat developers tend to use COTS or flight-proven solutions which usually have low testing coverage. Nowadays, there is still some pending matter in the field of testing nanosatellites flight software and some of the most used solutions do not even report unit tests. To overcome the agile CubeSat development versus delivering quality software trade-off, we propose the use of fuzz testing techniques applied to the SUCHAI series of nanosatellites, being developed at the University of Chile. The successful application of this technique allowed us to find and solve many bugs not covered by classic strategies, such as unit testing and software in the loop simulation.

articleTitle: Model Free DEAP Controller Learned by Reinforcement Learning DDPG Algorithm
abstract: In this work the Reinforcement Learning method is applied to construct a controller for Dielectric Electroactive Polymer actuator. The learning of control policy is model free without prior knowledge about the exact model of device dynamics. Due to the nonlinearities, multiple time constants and output feedback the control design is challenging task. To solve the problem, the recent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient is applied. Further, the controller is designed with and without model reference.

articleTitle: Development of a Wireless Traffic Light Controller System, with Real-Time Traffic Monitoring and Green Wave Coordination applied to Smart Cities
abstract: The accelerated urbanization process can cause several traffic problems, such as congestion, environmental, and noise pollution [1]-[3]. The system hardware developed consists of an actuator circuit, for the switching of AC/DC lamps and a sensor circuit, to check if the lamps are burnt out [4]. The microcontroller's firmware performs all the control logic, timing and traffic light safety for each type of crossing [5], [6]. For all traffic lights at all intersections to operate as intended, a wireless communication network with a specific communication protocol was used to mediate the information exchange between the traffic lights at intersections and its control center [7]. Safety routines [8]-[10] have been designed so that, in the event of technical problems (burnt-out lamp, electrical or communication failure) with one or more traffic lights at a given intersection, all traffic lights immediately go into alert mode and notify the situation to the traffic management center. The wireless traffic light controller system (according to Fig. 1) allows the green wave [11], [12] implementation for successive intersections. The system validation was based on the comparison of the theoretical and practical time diagrams, so that in all situations in which the system was exposed, it acted in the way it was designed.

articleTitle: Low Active and Reactive Power Reserve in Honduras Northwest’s Transmission System
abstract: During peak demand hours the Honduran northwestern transmission network experiences low voltage and high reactive power shortage issues. Because of this, three blackouts were reported in 2019. Installing power capacitors at the distribution level is not enough to solve these problems because the reactive power is needed at the transmission level (138 kV). Based on a dynamic power system analysis, this paper shows the investments that the transmission company should make to mitigate these problems. Results show that both the transmission network expansion and the installation of a Static VAr Compensator (SVC) are critical providing dynamic reactive power compensation to avoid voltage-collapse and get the generation costs reduced.

articleTitle: Development of an Indoor Hybrid PLC/VLC/IR Communication System based on TCP/IP Model
abstract: In this paper, we report the results obtained from the experimental implementation of a hybrid communication system, composed by: power line communication (PLC), visible light communication (VLC) and infrared light communication (IR). This hybrid PLC/VLC/IR system consists of an uplink and a downlink, allowing full-duplex communication between two personal computers. An important contribution is that it has been possible to integrate the hybrid system to the TCP/IP model through the use of a virtual network interface that allows communication between the elements of the physical layer with the upper layers present in the TCP/IP model. Additionally, USRP software defined radio platforms and the GNU Radio program are used for implementing physical layer. Performed measurements show that the entire system has a latency of 2.85 ms and a bandwidth of 29 kbps. However, using only VLC and IR, latency is reduced to 2.42 ms and the network bandwidth is increased to 2.45 Mbps.

articleTitle: Preliminary analysis of energy consumption in public buildings with IRAM-ISO 50001 approach. Case study: Faculty of Engineering Oberá
abstract: This work is framed in a research project applied to public buildings which was carried out in the field of the Faculty of Engineering of the UNaM. The research project seeks to analyze methodologies for the implementation of an Energy Management System based on IRAM ISO 50001/18 standards that contribute to the improvement of energy performance by reducing energy consumption. The energy sources currently used are electricity and fuel. The measurement limits include the Central Building, CEFI, Buffet, the Sports Centre and Patagonia Bank. All the electrical energy of these areas of the Faculty of Engineering is registered by one of the energy meters of the distributor. The annual energy registered by this meter in 2019 amounted to a value close to 115.6MW-hr, representing 47% of what was consumed by the institution in the 2019 period. For the 2019 period, the distributor's remaining meter registered an energy consumption close to 54%. This remaining meter records the energy of the Civil Engineering Building and its laboratories, which reached an annual consumption of 247MW-hr in 2019. Regarding the other energy source consumed for the university's activities, fuel, there are no concrete data. Part of the activities of the implementation of the EnMS includes the review and data collection of equipment that consumes energy in the Faculty. There is a record from the heritage of all the institution's equipment and tools, but not of their consumption and efficiency.In order to record why the high energy consumption is due even when the activities of the faculty are reduced, smart meters were installed in different circuits. This article presents power analysis results for one of these meters. It is detected that 42% of the energy consumption of this circuit occurs during night hours, where there are no work activities.

articleTitle: Automation of the short message service (SMS) delivery in a telecommunication company with Python and batch files
abstract: A Peruvian telecommunication company sends millions of SMS every day to promote their services through SMS mobile advertising. The workflow to deliver the SMS has the following processes: data collection, data preparation and delivery. Each process involves a variety of repetitive and monotonous tasks performed by the workers who have the goal of sending the SMS on time following a strategic schedule. When these tasks are performed entirely manually, they have a negative effect on the workers' performance, generate time pressure and create a bottleneck in the processes impacting the SMS-delivery schedule. To speed up the actual workflow, we automated each process with the use of batch files and the programming language Python, whose vast library helped us connect to the automating testing suite 'selenium'. As a result, the long-monotonous processes were simplified by simple scripts where a worker only had to introduce a few inputs to accomplish their task. With this automation, we reduced the total workflow time dramatically, making the SMS-delivery workflow smooth and straightforward.

articleTitle: Preliminary analysis of the new space communication scenario: the ground segment perspective
abstract: Miniaturized satellites are the protagonist of the New Space era. The current trend in this changing space sector corresponds to the deploy and operation of large satellite constellations consisting of hundreds or thousands of mini-, micro- or nanosatellites. Such a number of satellites have no precedents and propose new challenges both in space and ground segments. The ground segment, in particular, must manage the workload of serving current and future mega-constellations. A large amount of data storage and processing capabilities, agile steerable and multi-beam antennas, new ground station locations, and international cooperation are just some of the challenges to overcome. South America, especially countries at high latitudes, present excellent opportunities to deploy a ground station network prepared for this scenario. In this work, we execute a series of simulations to determine the number of satellites that need to be served by existing and potential ground station sites in Chile and Argentina. Results for constellations of sizes from 100 to 10,000 satellites show that around 10% to 20% of these satellites are passing over the ground stations per hour. We also discuss key technologies that may help to overcome these challenging scenarios.

articleTitle: Cargo Vehicle Classification System Through Axle Detection
abstract: A system capable of detecting trucks and their axles using convolutional neural networks (CNN) is presented. First, the system detects the trucks in an image by defining a bounding box around it and then proceeds to count the axles of the truck. The selected CNN models used for evaluation are the Faster R-CNN and Inception-ResNet V2 due to its performance according to the reviewed literature. For training and testing of the proposed solution a mobile unit was implemented to collect an image dataset consisting of trucks and other vehicles in a high-volume highway. Performance for this application was evaluated using different metrics resulting in a score of at least 92% in F1 Score, Recall and Precision.

articleTitle: Congestion Control Proposal in SDN With Random Early Detection
abstract: The emerging technology of SDN (Software Defined Networks) separates the data control plane from the forwarding plane while maintaining a centralized control of the network management. The SDN features require new traffic engineering techniques that exploit the global (centralized) network view, and the status and features of traffic flows. Our purpose is to perform traffic engineering in an SDN architecture, using the OpenFlow protocol capabilities and the potential of the SDN controller to collect operational data of the entire network, such as topology, latency, buffer utilization and frame sizes of the controlled devices in order to implement QoS. Considering that the performance of the network is an essential component of Quality of Service (QoS), and congestion is the main factor that affects it, this paper explores a method to search for alternative paths based on data from switches using the Random Early Detection (RED) congestion control mechanism.

articleTitle: Fabricación de PICs basados en SiN utilizando litografía por escritura directa con láser UV [Not available in English]
abstract: In this work, we present preliminary results obtained in the fabrication of photonic integrated circuits (PICs) based on silicon nitride platform. We use direct writing lithography with UV laser to define structures with sub-micrometric resolutions, demonstrating the feasibility of manufacturing PICs in the clean room facilities at Centro Atómico Constituyentes (CNEA). With this technology, we can develop PICs prototypes for a big variety of applications rapidly and at a low cost.

articleTitle: Frequency Multiplier for Pulsed Lasers Using PIC
abstract: Microwave photonics allows superior RF and microwave processing functionalities in comparison to all-electronic solutions. Optical Time Division Multiplexing and frequency multipliers are fundamental building blocks of microwave photonics for example in photonics implementations of radar systems. In this work we present the design and simulation of a frequency multiplier for a pulsed picosecond laser using silicon on insulator and silicon nitride technologies. We separately analyze the components of the multiplier and compare the performance for both technologies. The final circuits multiply the 100 MHz laser frequency by a factor of four obtaining a footprint of 1.65 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and 3.45 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> for silicon and silicon nitride, respectively. The resultant circuits are optimized to reduce the losses and the footprint and provide a simple solution for frequency multiplication in both, silicon and silicon nitride, platforms.

articleTitle: Data Transfer Rates in HFC Networks
abstract: Current access networks need to transmit data with increasingly higher rates. HFC (Hybrid Fiber Coaxial) networks offer growth capacity. To obtain maximal transfer rates, we propose releasing the 500 MHz spectrum -currently assigned to the transmission of analog and even digital television-, to convert HFC networks into entirely data networks, by using the first 200 MHz of the total spectrum for upstream, and from 258 MHz and up to 1.8 GHz for downstream. As the architecture of HFC networks must decrease the number of active amplifiers, we use an N + 0 design, which allows serving smaller service areas while decreasing the noise and distortion indexes. The DOCSIS 3.1 standard uses the OFDM (Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing) system for transmission in downstream and OFDMA (Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiple Access) for upstream, employing multiple sub-carrier schemes, each of which is modulated with up to 16K QAM in downstream and up to 4K QAM in upstream. Multiple modulation profiles (MMP) are associated to the quality of the channel. FEC-LDPC (Forward Error CorrectionLow Density Parity Check) is used for error correction. The maximal transfer rate calculated in downstream is 16.9 Gbps, and 1.86 Gbps in upstream. To achieve these values, it is necessary to maintain a SNR higher than 40 dB in the HFC network. In this way, HFC networks represent a valid alternative to meet demand for transfer rates in the short and medium term.

articleTitle: Tunable Microstrip Combline L-Band Filter Design, Fabrication and Characterization
abstract: A third order tunable microstrip combline bandpass filter is designed, simulated, fabricated and measured. Varactor diodes provides the electrical tuning, resulting in almost 1 GHz sweep range near the center of the L band. An alternative varactor feeding setup is proposed, which simplifies the fabrication and allows to increase the filter efficiency. A bandwidth of nearly 40 MHz, resulting in less than 3 % FBW is obtained. Insertion loss results in excess of 10 dB over the full sweep range. Filter performance hindrance is evaluated by adequately modeling varactors Q variation and its series resistance nonlinear behavior with frequency. Proper simulation through the use of the Spice model in co-simulation between 3D EM and nonlinear environment resulted of outmost need.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis in PMSM with Partitioned Stator Windings−Part I: Experimental Validation with Static Eccentricity
abstract: A signal-based strategy for static eccentricity (SE) detection in permanent magnet synchronous machines (PMSM) is proposed in this work. The effects of SE are analyzed from a model developed using a finite element method (FEM). SE detection is realized by evaluating the residual voltages (RV) obtained from the midpoint voltages measured in the middle of the windings of each phase. Unlike the methods based on motor current or voltage signature analysis (MCSA/MVSA), RVs allow to detect only the effects of an SE against other external problems that are usually found in industrial applications. Experimental laboratory results are presented which were obtained using bearings with eccentric bushings to generate different degrees of SE in the PMSM. The proposed strategy is validated by comparing the results obtained by FEM with the experimental tests for PMSM in different operating conditions, guaranteeing the correct diagnosis of SE.

articleTitle: Un análisis aproximado de la burbuja explosiva generada por liberación instantánea de energía [Not available in English]
abstract: Theoretical concepts and numerical formalisms used to approximately define the explosive bubble that can be generated by instantaneous release of energy are described. This energy is of such magnitude that it supports the use of theoretical concepts of strong shock waves, to determine the limits of bubble expansion. The properties of the gas contained inside, necessary when given the radius of the bubble and its expansion speed, it is desired to quantify the energy for its creation, are determined by applying the similar solution of Sedov and its presentation according to Hayes and Probstein.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Control With Space Vector Modulation for a Matrix Converter-fed Induction Machine
abstract: Matrix converters have been considered recently for several industrial and commercial applications, due to their lower size and weight and no dc-link requirement compared to the traditional back-to-back topology. As a consequence, several control techniques have been proposed for motor drives fed by matrix converters. The aim of this paper is to present a robust nonlinear control algorithm with a detailed description of the modulation stage for the current control of a three-phase induction machine. Simulation results explore the robustness of a sliding-mode based controller under perturbances and parameter mismatch.

articleTitle: Control of COVID-19 Outbreak for Preventing Collapse of Healthcare Capacity based on Social Distancing, Confinement and Testing-Quarantining
abstract: This work is a contribution to the call to The IFAC-CSS Corona Control Community Project in February 2020. Scientific evidence to the effectiveness of the three main non-pharmacological tools to mitigate a pandemic is given. A control system to control the Covid-19 outbreak caused by the Sars-CoV2 virus, called Coronavirus, is proposed, for preventing collapse of the health systems and saturation of Intensive Therapy Units (ITUs) capacity. The proposed system is based on the three existing non-pharmacological tools for the mitigation of epidemics and pandemics: social distancing, confinement and testing with isolation of a population in which there is community circulation of the virus. Both in the analysis and in the design of the control system, the mathematical model SEIRD (Susceptible - Exposed - Infected - Recovered - Deceased) is used, which describes the dynamics of a pandemic, adjusted in this work to the behavior in space and time of the Sars-CoV2. In this work the incidence and impact of testing with isolation (or testing-quarantining) is incorporated in the model. The proposed control system uses, as a feedback signal, the demanded quantity of critical beds and ITUs, which is compared with the available beds capacity to generate the error signal as input to a PID controller. As control actions, five Phases of Social Distancing and Confinement (SD&C) are proposed, which must be applied by the public authority. The control system thus generates a SD&C decision sequence or policy, which can be applied once a week or every fortnight. Simulation results showing the practical feasibility and good performance of the proposed control system are given, preventing collapse of Healthcare Capacity based on Social Distancing, Confinement and Testing-quarantining as control actions.

articleTitle: Implementation of a basic ADSL System using the DSP kit TMS320C6748
abstract: In this paper the implementation of a multi-carrier ADSL digital communication system in a TMS320C6748 DSP Development kit (LCDK) digital signal processor (DSP) is presented. QAM modulation / demodulation schemes, symbol timing and an equalization scheme are implemented. The information sent through the system is processed using cyclic redundancy check blocks, Scrambler and Reed-Solomon encoding. The operation of the system is verified experimentally by designating eight low frequency carriers and using the audio CODEC available in the DSP kit.

articleTitle: Monthly Deforestation Prediction using eXtreme Gradient Boosting based on MODIS EVI time series
abstract: The Dry Chaco region (DCF) has the highest absolute deforestation rates in Argentina. In this study, we evaluated the performance of the Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGboost) algorithm to detect breakpoint in MODIS EVI time series. The model takes as input 2-year long "time series segments". This process is usually seen as a breakpoint in the MODIS EVI time series, associated with the change from a forest phenology to something else (e.g. pasture, cropland). The model was validated using in situ data derived from high resolution images (Landsat 7 and 8). We also compared the performance of XGBoost to traditional machine learning models using classification. Finally, we evaluated feature importance using SHAP. This analysis provided evidence of how different sections of the segment would help to identify deforested pixels.

articleTitle: Feasibility of the inversion of electromagnetic models to estimate soil salinity using SAOCOM data
abstract: The present work evaluates the feasibility of the inversion of electromagnetic models in order to estimate soil salinity through the imaginary part of the dielectric constant using SAOCOM images (L-band, 1.275 GHz) over an agricultural area in Córdoba, Argentina. Considering that the real and imaginary part of the dielectric constant behave differently, SAR images can be exploited to detect soils affected by salts: while the real part is basically independent of soil salinity, the imaginary part is highly sensitive to variations of electrical conductivity, linked to the content of salts in the soil. This fact allows the identification of saline s oils from n on-saline s oils. The results obtained with empirically corrected POM model with SAOCOM data show promising results, with values of the imaginary part of the dielectric constant in non-saline validation sites in the range of 4.497 to 17.711, describing a framework towards future implementations of methodologies with SAR images for the detection and monitoring of this problematic.

articleTitle: Differential Current Monitoring for the Detection of Inter-Turns Short Circuits in Power Transformers
abstract: Inter-turns short circuits are a cause of failure that can result in high impact damage to the integrity of power transformers. Their early detection is essential to reduce repair and service interruption costs. One of the primary protections of power transformers are the conventional differential relays, which can detect inter-turns short circuits. However, if the fault involves a few turns, the differential relays are not able to detect it until the inter-turns short circuit progresses due to dielectric and thermal effects to a more severe fault. Therefore, it is of special interest to develop strategies that detect early-stage faults. These strategies can be supplementary and incorporated into the digital differential relays to improve their sensitivity. This paper proposes an algorithm for detecting inter-turns short circuits based on monitoring differential currents. From the analysis of the excitation currents of a power transformer, a single fault indicator applicable to differential currents is determined. Through laboratory experimental tests on a 10 kVA three-phase transformer specially designed to simulate faults, it was shown that for this case study the algorithm is sensitive to faults involving 1.5 to 3.3 % of the winding depending on the phase involved with a current in the fault loop of 1 pu. Moreover, the fault indicator is almost independent of the transformer's load condition, working from no-load condition to overload.

articleTitle: Benefits of using an audiobook application as an educational entertainment tool for children: a review of the scientific literature in the years 2006-2019
abstract: Virtual entertainment media have become essential for children, especially in times of confinement where some study virtually and others give their studies a break, a situation that is occurring worldwide due to the spread of COVID-19. This article shows the systematic review of the literature, synthesizing 32 articles, obtained from databases such as: IEEE Xplore, EBSCO, SCOPUS, ProQuest, among others. The objective of the article is to identify which are the benefits of using an audiobook application as a means of educational entertainment in children. It shows in results 18 benefits and 13 outstanding qualities that is why it is recommended its implementation in future research.

articleTitle: Estrategias docentes para la enseñanza remota implementadas en la Licenciatura en Sistemas de Información de la Universidad Nacional del Nordeste [Not available in English]
abstract: The COVID-19 Pandemic scenario had repercussions on the traditional teaching modality, triggering the implementation of actions to guarantee the continuity of the educational process. This work intends to address different aspects related to the strategies implemented for the teaching of the subjects of the Licenciarura de Información de la Facultad de Ciencias Exactas y Naturales y Agrimensura de la Universidad Nacional del Nordeste, in order to elucidate which pedagogical models emerge from the development of remote teaching processes. It is a descriptive study with a quantitative-qualitative approach. In order to carry it out, different data sources and collection instruments applied in the faculty's environment were used, as well as from the UNNE Virtual Program. What was observed allowed to identify the strategies developed by the teachers of the LSI, to recognize some strengths and limitations and, based on that, to propose some future lines of work.

articleTitle: Detection of Inter-turn Short Circuits in Power Transformers Windings:State of the Art
abstract: Currently, there are on-line and off-line application techniques for transformer fault diagnosis. Of these two modalities, off-line tests have traditionally been applied with greater recurrence. These tests have different purposes and can be classified as basic or advanced.In recent years, on-line fault detection and diagnosis strategies, based on the monitoring of electrical variables, have emerged with great potential to prevent transformer failures. These new techniques are based, for example, on the ratio of the increments of the flux linkages, locus diagram analysis, on the monitoring of variables obtained from the Park transform, on the monitoring of the transformer's positive sequence admittance or in the ratio of negative sequence currents. Such techniques have been implemented under very different conditions. The aim of this work is to present a conceptual comparison of the different alternatives found in the literature. The comparison focuses exclusively on inter-turns short circuit faults, since it is a fault component of considered recurrence in transformer windings.

articleTitle: Analysis and prevention of IoT vulnerabilities by implementing a lightweight AD-IoT intrusion detection system model
abstract: Until a few years, the Internet of Things (IoT) has been continually evolving and today it is giving a great welcome to a paradigmatic style of technology, for this reason new electronic devices are being invented that are used continuously by many people. But these devices must be protected in a certain way since there are many attacks on the IoT web, with which, by integrating new algorithms, certain network security will be obtained. In addition, the use of new model systems; such as the IoT Anomaly Detection System (AD-IoT) that uses the Random Forest (RF) machine learning algorithm to detect web attacks; It will help us reduce attacks from bad IoT computer users. In this present article, a very effective evaluative metric was obtained through a group of data that will help us develop and modify the communication security paradigms of IoT devices.

articleTitle: Multicriteria Analysis of the Opportunity Cost of the Sale of Paraguayan Energy from Itaipu to the Brazilian Market
abstract: The abundance of clean and renewable electrical energy constitutes a strategic asset for the development of the countries, and Paraguay has great availability of hydroelectric energy based on its participation in the binational power plants Itaipu and Yacyretá, in condominium with Brazil and Argentina.. However, a large part of the electricity production is not consumed in the country and is transferred to both Argentina and Brazil. In this sense, it is clear that the strategic use of the surplus of hydroelectricity that is currently being transferred could be key to lead the process of economic and social development in Paraguay, either by encouraging the consumption of its energy through the installation of industries, thus generating jobs and mobilizing the internal economy, or selling the surplus to third countries. Any selected alternative and the rejection of other alternatives will be inextricably linked to an opportunity cost. This work presents a methodology that allows identifying the opportunity cost of the sale of Paraguayan electricity to the Brazilian electricity market, with the use of the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP). It was possible to determine energy sales prices in the Brazilian market, for which rents would be generated that would significantly affect the development of Paraguay, ranging from US $63,55/MWh to US $2.841/MWh. It can be concluded that a scenario of high export of Paraguayan hydroelectric energy to Brazil presents an opportunity cost, for several scenarios where decision makers have a notorious predilection for the Economic, Environmental and Social criteria, in addition to some combinations of these criteria with others.

articleTitle: A data-driven approach to weather forecast using convolutional neural networks
abstract: The Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) Model is a numerical weather prediction system designed for both atmospheric research and operational forecasting applications. WRF can produce simulations based on actual atmospheric conditions or idealized conditions and provide forecasts such as precipitation and geopotential height among others. This paper addresses the analysis of the influence of these variables on rain condition in order to complement the WRF model precipitation forecast. Convolutional neural networks (CNN), used in the field of image processing, were applied to develop a machine learning model that takes the data generated by the WRF model as an input and capture the relationship with measured precipitation data. This process resulted in two models that achieved a rain prediction with an accuracy of about 80%. This results prove the capacity of the model to learn the existing correlation between the input variables and actual data. However, they also revealed the need for data that span a time interval that includes the different existing cycles (e.g. solar cycles) in order to make further reliable predictions.

articleTitle: Core Loss Prediction in Power Electronic Converters Based on Steinmetz Parameters
abstract: Based on a modification of the Steinmetz equation, simple and general formulas suitable for magnetic power loss estimation in converter design are proposed. Using only the manufacturer data sheet parameters for sinusoidal waveforms, it is possible to estimate the core losses in symmetrical converters. A loss model is introduced to consider the loss increment caused by DC magnetization bias in asymmetrical converters, giving worst case criteria to design the magnetic components.

articleTitle: Stability Analysis Of Locomotion Using Normalized Dynamic Energy Stability Margin For a Hexapod Robot ROMERIN
abstract: Walking robots are used in hard to reach places, as military missions, mining, among others, however, these robots need maintain the stability during their displacement by use of a dynamic stability margin. In this paper, The Normalized Dynamic Energy Stability Margin is applied in order to study the stability of locomotion for hexapod robot ROMERIN, with a tripod gait in a flat horizontal surface. The parameters that affect stability were identified, the configuration adopted by the links of the robot is characterized by step length, the maximum height of displacement of the leg end in stride phase, and the maximum distance of displacement of the legs in stride phase to the outside of the body, in addition a key factor is the speed of displacement, the step length is selected who maximizes it and find the average velocity close to stability loss, under specific conditions.

abstract: Energy efficiency can be applied in buildings and industries, resulting in the minimization of CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> in the environment and economic savings for the user. This project analyzes the consumption of the pumping system used to supply the water flow demanded in San Nicolás de los Arroyos. This study is carried out over a period of one year. During that period of time, the corresponding consumption of the power service contracted and the power factor of each group of pumps were analyzed. However, this is made the economic comparation between the years 2018 and 2020. The results obtained indicate a high number of pumps with defective contracts and a low power factor.

articleTitle: Assesing the entry of PV generation in subsystems of the National Interconnected System from Paraguay
abstract: This work seeks to develop an equivalent model of Paraguay's National Interconnected System (SIN), organized in six subsystems and with an hourly time resolution, in order to quantify the economic impact associated to the entry of PV projects in terms of savings in operating costs. Paraguay accounts for PV generation potential over almost the entire country. Hence, PV projects distributed throughout the country's regions could help in reducing transmission congestion and losses, having in mind the demand growth and the fact that currently generation and consumption centers are rather distant from one another. The model development is based of hourly-equivalent curves for the demand and the PV generation, by considering a typical installed capacity, in each subsystem of the SIN. The simulation period extends for 10 years, from 2018 to 2028, and five scenarios for the demand growth rate are analyzed. For simulating the SIN's operation and performing power flow calculations, the MATPOWER extension for MATLAB is used. Simulation results, obtained by assuming the entry of a typical PV project in one subsystem at the time, allow to rank the subsystems in terms of operating costs reduction. In that sense, it is concluded that the entry of the PV project in the Southern Subsystem implies the most-feasible investment alternative.

articleTitle: OpenWee, Opensource Wind energy empowerment
abstract: OpenWee is an opensource device for low power wind applications with the ability to work as a wind regulator, automatic brake and also a system datalogger. The wind regulator contemplates after three phases of charging a battery, in bulk (bulk), absorption and float, allowing it to extend its useful life. The automatic brake is activated by stopping the wind turbine when a voltage above the regulation references is exceeded, working as a protection, it is also possible to activate it manually by means of a switch. Finally, the datalogger allows you to monitor different sensor variables and store them via Wi-Fi in a database in the cloud, to later be able to view them via cell phone or PC. The potential of OpenWee resides in that being opensopurce gives the possibility of adapting it depending on the application, including different sensors, also its low cost allows reaching an affordable device for rural communities that are low-income.

articleTitle: Analysis of a single-phase AC-AC SST and a grid filter design methodology
abstract: This work presents the analysis of a single-phase, single-stage AC-AC solid-state transformer, in conjunction with a switching strategy using phase-shift modulation. A grid filter design methodology is also proposed to minimize the harmonic content in the phase currents of interconnected grids. By means of the phase shift between the voltages applied to the high- frequency transformer terminals of the converter, it is possible to control the power flow in a bidirectional mode and obtain currents with low harmonic distortion and a power factor close to unity in both grids for almost the entire active power transfer operating range. A theoretical analysis is carried out and the results obtained are validated by means of numerical simulations.

abstract: This article presents a modular equipment that allows the implementation of single-phase or three-phase power electronics topologies for research applications. The designed equipment includes an interface to adaptation of signals that is compatible with Digital Signal Controllers (DSC) models TMS320F28377D and TMS320F28335. In addition, drivers compatible with uni-directional or bi-directional power devices were designed, and a Power Module that integrates on a single board the voltage and current measurement circuits, power devices, DC link (Direct Current) and capacitor bank. Finally, an example of implementation of a single-phase Dual Active Bridge (DAB) DC-DC converter is presented with its experimental results.

articleTitle: Computer security in the emerging technologies of the Internet of Things
abstract: Until a few years ago the internet could only be used through a computer and mobile devices such as smartphones, today many objects can be interconnected using the internet, including televisions, washing machines, smart lights, coffee makers, refrigerators, among others, this technology is called IOT (Internet of Things) which monitor, control, optimize and automate information in real time, this information is periodically stored in applications that help control IOT devices, the information received by the device contains personal data such as eating habits, Routine work and even banking credentials, this massive processing of data on the network can lead to attacks and the receipt of data for criminal or harmful purposes for the user. This article demonstrates the infrastructure used for data collection, where it can be configured with the help of protocols for the security of IOT device communications.

articleTitle: SafeSwim: Overhead vision to help people see better
abstract: Traditionally video surveillance consists of overhead cameras to help authorities such as lifeguards or security professionals monitor individuals. This monitoring, if in service of the monitored individuals, serves them only indirectly. More recently, a new kind of sensing called "sousveillance" has emerged, as a form of sensing by, and in direct service to, individuals. In this paper, we explore an overhead camera (e.g. aerial drone-based videography) to help create a form of real-time seeing aid, with specific application to help one or more individual swimmers see better and navigate, e.g. to avoid collisions with other swimmers (or the walls) in pools, as well as navigating in lakes, rivers, and other bodies of open water. Additionally the system can be used to teach swimming (e.g. learn by seeing from a birds-eyeview) as well as to gamify swim-based activities. SafeSwim (and sousveillance in general) is a new form of "seeing" in which those being watched have direct visual access to the live video stream. It is a direct departure from traditional surveillance where authorities such as police or lifeguards watch individuals without giving them direct access to a live video stream.

articleTitle: Control of COVID-19 Outbreak for Preventing Collapse of Healthcare Capacity based on Social Distancing, Confinement and Testing-Quarantining
abstract: This work is a contribution to the call to The IFAC-CSS Corona Control Community Project in February 2020. Scientific evidence to the effectiveness of the three main non-pharmacological tools to mitigate a pandemic is given. A control system to control the Covid-19 outbreak caused by the Sars-CoV2 virus, called Coronavirus, is proposed, for preventing collapse of the health systems and saturation of Intensive Therapy Units (ITUs) capacity. The proposed system is based on the three existing non-pharmacological tools for the mitigation of epidemics and pandemics: social distancing, confinement and testing with isolation of a population in which there is community circulation of the virus. Both in the analysis and in the design of the control system, the mathematical model SEIRD (Susceptible - Exposed - Infected - Recovered - Deceased) is used, which describes the dynamics of a pandemic, adjusted in this work to the behavior in space and time of the Sars-CoV2. In this work the incidence and impact of testing with isolation (or testing-quarantining) is incorporated in the model. The proposed control system uses, as a feedback signal, the demanded quantity of critical beds and ITUs, which is compared with the available beds capacity to generate the error signal as input to a PID controller. As control actions, five Phases of Social Distancing and Confinement (SD&C) are proposed, which must be applied by the public authority. The control system thus generates a SD&C decision sequence or policy, which can be applied once a week or every fortnight. Simulation results showing the practical feasibility and good performance of the proposed control system are given, preventing collapse of Healthcare Capacity based on Social Distancing, Confinement and Testing-quarantining as control actions.

articleTitle: Industrial Symbiosis: Context-Aware Strategies for Automated Negotiation of Smart Contracts in Peer-to-Peer Markets of Prosumers
abstract: Industrial Symbiosis can evolve from a simple concept to a revolutionary practical approach where prosumer companies produce goods and provide services through automated negotiation of Smart Contracts by means of new technologies like Internet-of-Things (IoTs) and Blockchain in a Peer-to-Peer (P2P) Market. However, a symbiotic scheme of prosumers exchanging utility surpluses and industrial services gives rise to a great challenge: each company will only participate in the market if the motivation of increasing its own profits exists. I n t his work, each prosumer company is represented by a software agent that resorts to previously learned context-aware strategies for defining prior distributions. Then, strategies are adapted to different opponents when negotiating utility contracts by properly accounting for opponents’ preferences (private) and key contextual (public) information. Agents negotiating Smart Contracts can be readily implemented using Distributed Applications (dApps) over Ethereum/Solidity and digital currencies as the Ether.

articleTitle: On Machine Learning Methods for Genome Enabled Prediction of Complex Phenotypes
abstract: We present a video outlining the potential of applying machine learning techniques to genome enabled prediction of complex phenotypes with agricultural value, in a context of increasing genetic data availability. It is part of an ongoing research project on the subject, and aims to introduce the problem and main motivations behind this line of research to other researchers and the general public.

articleTitle: Indoor Harvesting RF Energy System Applied to Low Consumption Wireless Devices
abstract: This work discusses the development and the results of the tests of a prototype for a POC (Proof of Concept) of an Indoor RF Harvesting Energy System that can be used to charge wireless devices, including mobile ones, which are inside of a closed room properly prepared for this purpose. EMC concepts were considered in the layout of the circuits and in the assembly of the receiving section, as well as in the tests performed. The study presented here is a charging option for devices that consume low power while charging. The system can operate in the bandwidths of 1 MHz and 150 MHz depending on the applications and the dedicated components that are used in each case. Basically it consists of the transmitting and receiving circuits, with their respective antennas, a power conversion module and a special circuit responsible for delivering and managing the charging of the load of the wireless device. The system operates in near and far field regions, depending on the frequency and the distance between the transmitter and the receiver from 1 to 3m.

articleTitle: Optimal Transmission Switching for cost reduction in the Interconnected System of Paraguay
abstract: Traditionally, transmission assets are characterized for being fixed assets, and they are built based on redundancy to manage different scenarios in the long term, but this type of view can create congestion in some lines and increase the operation cost in the short run due to generation re-dispatch or load shed. Therefore, the Optimal Transmission Switching proposed takes into account the co-optimization of the generators dispatch and the network configuration, intending to reduce operation costs. Consequently, this paper presents a methodology to look for network configurations that reduce the operation costs, the considered case of study is the Interconnected System of Paraguay. Since the network reconfiguration represents a combinatorial problem, a methodology based on genetic algorithms is proposed as an optimization strategy. Finally, it was found that savings up to 1700 USD/h and power losses reduction around 10% can be achieved, all of them considering a safe operation.

articleTitle: Study of hydro-snowy dynamics in the Mendoza Andes using SAR data, optical data and gauging stations
abstract: Snow is an essential parameter of the cryosphere and plays a fundamental role in the hydrological cycle, therefore monitoring of the snow is of great importance specially with regard to irrigation, hydroelectric power generation, and for human consumption and production. Satellite Remote Sensing, with both optical and Synthetic Aperture Radars (SAR) instruments, can provide distributed observations of snow cover over extended and inaccessible areas such as the Andes. In this study through optical data Landsat 8, snow cover area was obtained, then applying the change detection method developed by Nagler y Rott (2000), Sentinel 1 data was used for wetsnow classification. With the cartography and with data from the gauging stations, hidro-snowy seasonal dynamics was analyzed. The study was carried out in The Andes in the province of Mendoza over the Río Mendoza and Río Tunuyán basins. The results obtained show the relevance of the satellite sensors to determine the snow cover and to estimate with SAR images, the wet snow, which represents a flow input to the rivers and reservoirs located downstream.

abstract: This paper presents the procedure carried out to establish the requirements of electrical and mechanical power for an international railway service, developed between the cities of Posadas, Argentina and Encarnación, Paraguay. The main objective is to propose a technical specification for a project in order to implement electrification of this railway, so the service can be achieved by using electric trains. Simulation results of the power requirements necessary for the operation of the electric train are presented.

articleTitle: Test of Emergency Generation System for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
abstract: Summary: After the first flight tests of the UAV prototype called LCA-FICA-X03 whose mission is to travel great distances, we saw the need to have an energy microgrid installed in it, with an emergency generation system that It was independent of any condition, be it environmental or the time of day, and a generation system was thought of that is low weight, low power and low cost that can power the UAV flight for its return home in an emergency. The idea is that the electric motor is used at first as a starter, and once the combustion engine starts, it goes to its function as a generator. A stand for the generator is designed and built and various laboratory tests are done until it can be tested with the UAV in flight.

articleTitle: Energy Efficiency of Street Lighting in the Municipality of Villa Mercedes, San Luis
abstract: In this descriptive work, secondary information from the sub-secretariat of Control and Execution of Public Works of the Municipality of Villa Mercedes is analyzed in the period 2017 to 2019, the use of new technologies is proposed to mitigate the consumption of public lighting (AP). The data collection technique was documentary since the documentary review and analysis of the reports presented was carried out. As results, the actions and improvements related to the PA carried out during the 2018-2019 period are presented. The first results of the replacement by LED luminaires show that a reduction of more than 35% was achieved in a main avenue of the city. An economic analysis is proposed to improve in the period 2020-2025.

articleTitle: Evaluation of long-term energy efficiency measures in transport: case study Paraguay
abstract: Paraguay is one of the world's largest exporters of electrical energy. Although, its energy matrix depends mainly on biomass and hydrocarbons, the latter being imported. Based on this, this study evaluated efficiency measures for the main final use of hydrocarbons identified, namely long-distance land transport of cargo. Long-term diesel and electric rail transport scenarios were studied, using an energy model developed in the Long-range Energy Alternatives Planning software and an energy, economic and environmental (related with emission savings) analysis was carried out. The results obtained show the great potential for economic, energy and environmental savings with the application of measures to replace end-use and primary energy source technologies in the long term, in all branches of energy demand

articleTitle: Analytical Modeling of Unequal Tooth Width Permanent Magnet Machines
abstract: This paper presents an alternative for the analytical modeling of permanent magnet machines with concentrated windings and fractional pitch using unequal teeth widths distribution. This proposal is based on the characterization of the functions of the windings distribution and flux distribution, carried on by Fourier series approximations. This model is finally validated using Finite Element Analysis.

articleTitle: Robust Virtual Impedance Droop Control for Reactive Power Sharing in Microgrids
abstract: The stability and accurate load sharing among distributed generators (DG) in a microgrid is dependent on the control strategy employed. Droop control is the commonly used technique. The active and reactive power are coupled in a microgrid due to its resistive nature. The terminal voltage of the DG is a local parameter. It depends on the local loads and impedance mismatch of lines. The inaccurate reactive power sharing among DGs is caused by the line impedance mismatches. A robust virtual impedance droop controller is proposed to match the line impedances and to maintain the voltage constant. The introduction of virtual impedance makes the microgrid inductive that helps to decouple the power. The robust controller in conjunction with the impedance controller maintain the output voltage constant by employing an automatic gain controller and shares the reactive power according to DGs rated capacity. The implementation of the controller is practically viable as it requires slight modifications to the conventional droop scheme. To verify the accuracy and viability of robust virtual impedance control strategy, simulations are performed on MATLAB/Simulink. The system performance is analysed during transition from grid connected mode to islanded mode and during load changes in islanded mode operation.

articleTitle: Geolocation tool for limiting the multiple estimation problem of fault location in rural electric power distributors considering load flow calculations in branch lines
abstract: This paper presents a geographical information system-based computational tool for fault location in rural medium voltage radial overhead electrical distribution systems. The software includes algorithms that limit the multiple estimation problem when locating the failure. In order to identify the real location of the fault among the ones found as electrically equivalent, the proposed methodology compares each voltage and current values on each section of the network identified as a possible faulted line section. The decision that determines the real location of the fault is taken by calculating an error considering both their physical features and their load flow. This comparison is made on the basis of the estimated load flows of each branch belonging to the main distributor. The tool was validated by modelling a real distributor belonging to an electric power cooperative, in a simulation program of electric power systems. In this program, different types of short circuits are simulated to extract the necessary input data for the developed algorithm which estimates the possible failure points. In order to reconstruct the network, the program allows to recover its technical and topological data contained in the georeferenced data bases of the distribution companies approved by the Electric Regulation Entity of the Province of Buenos Aires, Argentina. The presentation of the results in a graphical environment of the network offers operators a quick and clear interpretation of possible fault locations, leading to a reduction in repair times and improving the quality of electricity service. The evaluation of the developed tool has shown a great precision locating the faults, with an error of less than 1%. For three-phase, two-phase and single-phase faults on three-wire lines, the problem of multiple estimation was narrowed down with an efficiency of 87%.

articleTitle: Dynamics of generation investments under uncertainty in the Paraguayan power system
abstract: In recent years, the demand of electricity in Paraguay has grown steadily. Thanks to large generation work, among which are binational companies, currently the installed capacity reserve margin is sufficient to serve the demand. However, projections indicate that this reserve margin would be exhausted in the medium term, so it is appropriate to analyze the viability of new investments in generation in order to accompany the growth in demand. In this sense, the decision to invest in generation plants, due to their characteristics, is made difficult due to the unpredictability in the growth of demand. In this sense, the use of simulation models is very useful to study the variables of the system and their evolution over time. This work is based on the Systems Dynamics simulation approach (SD), which allows representing the complexities of investments in generation considering a value of flexibility in said investments through the Real Options (RO) technique, taking as a case study to the Paraguayan electrical system. Although it has been found that generation expansion models based on DS are normally applied to deregulated electricity markets with a mostly thermal generation technologies, this work proposes an alternative since the Paraguayan electricity system is characterized by being vertically integrated and with a purely hydroelectric generation park. The development of this work reveals that it is feasible to study the evolution of installed generation capacity based on the uncertain growth of demand in vertically integrated electricity markets with a purely renewable generation park.

articleTitle: Real-time urban environmental map generation from mini mobile environmental stations based on Arduino Uno
abstract: This work includes the design and development of a real time web system for the generation of urban environmental maps from the capture of data of environmental parameters through low cost meteorological mini-stations assembled with Arduino technology and environmental quality sensors (Internet of things), this in order to obtain reports about the environmental status of the urban area of the district of Punchana. This work arises as an alternative to the problem of the scarce data for the study of the climatic change and the natural phenomena associated to these, that come giving along the time in Peru, besides being a system of low cost that allows its production in mass with regard to the traditional meteorological stations that are used at the present time by diverse institutions of the environment. For the purpose of the study, six environmental parameters were considered, suggested by SENAMHI experts. Thus, it was defined to study the levels of Carbon Dioxide (CO2), Liquid Petroleum Gas (LPG), Smoke, Environmental Temperature (°C), Relative Humidity and Ultraviolet Radiation. This work allowed checking the efficiency of data capture through low-cost meteorological mini-stations and the generation of environmental maps where the environmental status of the urban area of Punchana, Loreto, Peru, can be seen reflected, besides being a base work for later works involving environmental monitoring services.

articleTitle: Joint Angle Estimation with VIBE: an Evaluation Using Virtual Avatars
abstract: Work-related musculoskeletal disorders (WMSD) are health problems of the human locomotion system caused or intensified by inadequate work activities or environments. The usual alternative to prevent WMSDs is to implement an ergonomics program, which must include an evidence-based ergonomic risk assessment to recognize and rectify ergonomic deficiencies in a wide range of workplace situations. Ergonomic risk assessment is done traditionally through the completion of specific forms, through in-site observation by ergonomists. This is inaccurate and inefficient due to subjective biases. Also, it is not practical due to the cost, time, and technical knowledge required. For this reason, in this work we propose the standardization of data collection through computer vision, which offers the opportunity to obtain a considerable replication level, increasing the reliability of the results and the quality of the data available to ergonomists. As a methodology, we propose using the open-source neural network VIBE to detect skeletal joints in photos whose purpose is to calculate ergonomic risk. As an approach to rich and reliable data gathering, we carried out a virtual experiment, using controlled avatars in the Unity game engine. This allowed us to explore and quantify acquisition performances, in particular the occlusion effects generated by varying the camera angles concerning the worker’s bodies, and the errors induced by background clutter.

articleTitle: Weather Radar Parameters Obtained Through an MoM Simulation Validated with Real Data of Hydrometeors
abstract: We present here the development of a rain sample model, based on real data of hydrometeors and simulate the response of this sample to a radar signal using the Method of Moments. The data used to create the model have details about the geometry and velocity of raindrops. After that, we compare the simulation results with reliable data in an attempt to validate this model for more accurate and elaborated studies of the polarization parameters and for search others and better ways to determine meteor characteristics.The response of the rain model to the electromagnetic wave is evaluated in terms of Reflectivity Factor and Differential Reflectivity, two of the most frequently used parameters in the meteorological radar area, to characterize the meteor subject of the measurement. The results are validated with data provided with the rain data source, obtained using 2D Video Disdrometers and real radar data obtained for place and time of the used sample of rain.

articleTitle: Systematic Literature Review of Water-Energy Nexus: An Overview of the field and analysis of the top 50 influential papers
abstract: Water needs energy and energy needs water. In this context, the optimization of the use of each of these variables is a fundamental goal to tackle climate change and achieve sustainable development. The water-energy nexus has gained relevance in the literature through the study of their dependencies, with the objective of increasing their synergies and reducing their trade-offs. Moreover, the nexus approach has proven to be a useful methodology to evaluate the impact of a variable (or group of variables) in a specific system or network, as for example, the intricate network of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDG). The main purpose of this study is to improve the understanding of the water-energy nexus through a comprehensive literature review, based on the influence of the publications (citation-based approach). The methodology allows the identification of the top 50 most influential papers related to the water-energy nexus, based on the number of citations that it has, since its publication in a scientific journal. Additionally, it has been analyzed the main journals in this topic, the context and characteristics of the publications (geographical locations and study design), most cited authors, the timeline and evolution of the literature. Finally, the study seeks to improve the comprehension of the relevance of the dependencies and interactions between these variables, added to their fundamental roles in the whole system.

articleTitle: FCS-MPC Based Fault Tolerant Control for Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machines
abstract: In the present work, a fault-tolerant control strategy based on the predictive control by finite state model for permanent magnet synchronous machines is proposed. The behavior of the strategy is analyzed in a 4-wire topology. In this topology the neutral point of the machine is connected to the midpoint of a bank of direct current capacitors. The advantage of the strategy proposed in this document resides in the control scheme, which allows stable operation through a fault without the need to reconfigure either the inverter topology or the structure of the control algorithm. In this way, transients and the use of additional hardware components are avoided. The experimental results, obtained from a laboratory prototype, validate the practical viability of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: Assistive Technology Device for People with Autism
abstract: The research project had its development in the Assistive Technology area, which is the use of equipment, resources or strategies aimed at improving the functional skills of people with special needs. The researches were carried out about the behaviors of people with Autistic Spectrum Disorder (ASD), who show signs of social isolation, language problems and repetitive attitudes. These behaviors make the ASD sufferer have learning difficulties. In the psychological procedures carried out in clinics, psycho pedagogical centers and schools, teaching practices for patients with ASD are carried out, professionals carry out interventions and record the results manually to later formulate strategies aimed at the evolution of the patient.In this way, the monitoring of the treatment ends up being compromised, since even with the presence of the professional it is difficult to guide the patient in the activity, report errors, successes and record them manually. In addition, the support of activities ends up being restricted to clinics, since the professional is unable to monitor the activities performed at home with the patient every day, causing a certain discontinuity in the learning process.In this context there has been development of an embedded system containing a mobile application and an interactive panel to assist in the treatment of the people with autism. The methodology chosen for learning was Alternative Communication, where images were used; through the illustrations a tutorial on how to wash your hands in a simple way step by step. In the office with the help of the professional responsible for the treatment, the panel will be used to record the patient's time and errors during the activity, these records will be sent to the google drive and can be accessed later. The ESP32 microcontroller is being used to develop the panel, which has a Real time clock module and a Wi-Fi module embedded. These tools will help in the activity, because the time will be registered and sent to the Google Drive database. The mobile application is developed to complement the activities at home, where the user can exercise their memory by placing the images of the activity in the correct order. At the end, the father, mother or guardian fills in a small report with observations of the user's behavior during the activity which is sent to Google Drive. To develop this application, the React Native framework has been used, which uses the JavaScript language and allows the application to be compatible with android and IOS. The system's registration resources on the Google Drive will play an important role in the treatment of patients with autism, because with the data collected during the activities, it will be possible to assess the patient's condition and formulate new strategies for improving performance. The mobile application is functional and ready for testing with users, but the panel still needs further laboratory tests with the microcontroller. In the flowchart presented, it is possible to follow the principle of operation of the interactive panel.

articleTitle: Negotiation of Electricity Supply Capacities through a Double Auction Mechanism
abstract: This article considers a competitive negotiation of supply capacities among some enterprises and an electricity distribution company. An available dynamic negotiation strategy based on a double auction mechanism is utilized to investigate two kinds of cases: (i) one or more enterprises present an inelastic demand; and (ii) the negotiation framework is affected by the number of enterprises. Several study cases are simulated. The obtained results suggest that there are no individual or collective economic incentives to adopt an inelastic demand; and a joint benefit is achieved for all the involved enterprises (i.e., the industries and the energy distribution company) even increasing the number of enterprises. Results could be of interest for enterprises located e.g. in an industrial park.

articleTitle: Analysis of Professional Skills Using Growing Hierarchical Self-Organizing Map
abstract: With the increase of competitiveness among companies, knowledge management has become a strategic factor to ensure the sustainability of organizations. One of the most challenging problems within knowledge management is the representation of tacit knowledge, the subjective specialty, and the skills of a professional team. Many approaches have been proposed to store, represent, and retrieve tacit knowledge, but most fail on providing a sustainable and adaptable solution. In this paper, this problem was addressed by proposing a Growing Hierarchical Self-Organizing Map neural network to map the tacit knowledge from an organization in an unsupervised and hierarchical manner. It was introduced a novel relevance gain function, to process symbolic data, and find that our neural network can model the tacit knowledge of a real business.

articleTitle: Contractive Method for Identification of Nonlinear Regressors in Dynamic Systems
abstract: In this work, a method is exposed that allows the calculation of the parameters of non-linear regressors, of dynamic systems with intervals. The proposed method is a contractive method applicable to homeomorphic transformations. This requirement is met by many regressors used to model nonlinear dynamic systems. It allows to apply a model that can establish and make compatible four aspects: prediction horizon, uncertainty, data required for adjustment and validity domain. In other words, capturing the trend with a validity domain greater than that obtained with an adjustment of a greater number of parameters and less uncertainty. It has a robust character of its convergence. As a counterpart, it is a costly method in computational terms, but this circumstance is saved by its characteristic of parallelizable algorithms. In this way, it can be applied in a control system, with massive shutdown hardware.
